data.title: Kuaishou Earnings Call Signals AI Growth, Near-Term Pressure
data.description:
Kuaishou Technology Class B ((HK:1024)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Kuaishou’s third-quarter earnings call delivered a mixed message. The company highlighted progress in AI, user engagement, gaming, overseas e-commerce and shareholder returns, but weaker revenue, profit, margins and advertising demand showed that near-term conditions remain difficult.

Large User Base Remains Resilient

Kuaishou’s average daily active users reached 417 million in the quarter, up 0.3% from a year earlier. Monthly active users rose 12% to 819 million, although average daily time spent per user declined as competition intensified.

Shareholder Returns Continued

Kuaishou repurchased about 39.13 million shares for approximately HKD 1.41 billion in the third quarter. During the first three quarters of 2026, dividends and buybacks totaled about HKD 5.86 billion, with 70.14 million shares repurchased.

Strong Cash Resources

Cash, time deposits, financial assets and restricted cash totaled RMB 127.2 billion as of September 30, 2026. The substantial liquidity gives Kuaishou room to fund AI investment while continuing shareholder returns.

Kling AI Advances With New Model

Kling AI launched its next-generation Kling 4.0 model with up to 30-second native video generation, multi-frame control and multimodal reference input. The model was fully rolled out on October 15, while its application programming interface became available globally on October 28.

Kling AI Monetization Gains Momentum

Kling AI’s gross billings increased after the Kling 4.0 launch. Management said growth is being driven by enterprise API demand and paid consumer subscriptions, with user scale and average revenue per user also gaining across entertainment, advertising, e-commerce and gaming.

Creative Industries Validate Kling AI

Film, television, advertising and animation teams gave positive feedback on Kling 4.0. The tool is being used for storyboarding, previsualization, stylized content, advertising production, gaming and applications involving embodied intelligence.

AI Deployment Spreads Across Kuaishou

Kuaishou is applying AI across content, commerce and internal operations. GoalRank improved recommendation efficiency without additional inference computing, while generative recommendation, AIGC, intelligent bidding, AI agents, MyFlicker 2.0 and team-specific workflows were also deployed.

Vanchin Revenue Accelerates

Revenue from Kuaishou Vanchin, the company’s AI infrastructure platform, rose nearly 90% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter. The growth signals increasing demand for Kuaishou’s cloud and computing capabilities as AI usage expands.

Private Messaging Engagement Improved

The average daily number of users with mutual followers who engaged in private messaging increased more than 7% year-over-year. Daily users interacting through Huozaizai also exceeded 46 million, pointing to deeper social activity on the platform.

Content and Sports Attracted Large Audiences

The 2026 Kuaishou Super Summer Gala generated more than 200 million cumulative livestream views. Sports initiatives linked to the Asian Games produced over 19.5 billion cumulative short-video views, strengthening Kuaishou’s content reach.

Lord of the Mysteries Launches Strongly

Kuaishou’s in-house MMORPG Lord of the Mysteries attracted more than 1 million users in its first hour and reached peak concurrent users of 700,000. It topped mainland China’s App Store free-game chart for several days and showed strong conversion among paying users.

Short-Play Ecosystem Expands Rapidly

The average daily number of active short plays grew more than 350% between January and September 2026. Spending on online marketing services in the content-consumption sector increased more than 100% year-over-year in the third quarter, supported by rising supply and demand.

Marketing Tools Gain Adoption

The penetration rate of the Net Transaction ROI product rose to 34.7% from 28% in the second quarter. Both client and spending penetration for Universal Auto X exceeded 90%, while average daily spending on AIGC short-video marketing materials grew 20% year-over-year.

Brand Merchant Supply Broadens

New stores opened under brand matrix accounts increased more than 50% year-over-year. Kuaishou also reported steady quarter-over-quarter improvements in new merchant retention and the number of existing merchants reaching scaled growth.

AI E-Commerce Solution Shows Early Promise

Kuaishou introduced a fully managed AI operations solution for small and medium-sized e-commerce merchants. The service combines content creation, distribution and scenario-specific support, and generated initial business gains during the quarter.

Livestreaming Engagement Remains Active

The music livestreaming show Singing in the Mountains generated more than 270 million views by its finale. Kuaishou also used Fan Farm, improved recommendations and AI-generated interactive features to strengthen relationships between streamers and users.

Overseas E-Commerce Scales Profitably

Overseas e-commerce delivered solid year-over-year growth in gross merchandise volume and orders in the third quarter. Management said profitability and efficiency were maintained through local content, KOL-led transactions, better merchant and product mix, and higher average order values.

Flexible Computing Plans Could Improve Efficiency

Kuaishou has already secured substantial computing capacity for 2026, while Kling AI will use a more flexible mix of purchases and leasing. Management expects better allocation and engineering improvements to raise utilization and help control capital expenditure.

Buyback Program Remains in Place

Kuaishou plans to continue its HKD 16 billion, three-year share repurchase program. It will assess buybacks, dividends and other return methods according to business performance, cash flow and market conditions.

Revenue and Profit Fell

Third-quarter revenue declined to RMB 31.6 billion from RMB 35.6 billion a year earlier. Adjusted net profit fell to RMB 790 million, while adjusted EBITDA decreased to RMB 3.9 billion, reflecting pressure across the operating businesses.

User Time Spent Declined

Average daily time spent per daily active user decreased year-over-year in the third quarter. Management attributed the change mainly to stronger competition, despite the continued expansion of Kuaishou’s overall user base.

Online Marketing Revenue Weakened

Online marketing services revenue fell to RMB 17.9 billion from RMB 20.1 billion a year earlier. The decline was mainly caused by lower e-commerce marketing spending amid cautious consumption and increasingly intense competition.

E-Commerce Faced Broad Pressure

E-commerce gross merchandise volume and marketing services revenue both declined year-over-year. Cautious consumers, higher merchant operating and compliance costs, reduced subsidies for some products and more conservative marketing budgets weighed on activity.

Merchant Support Created Near-Term Trade-Offs

Kuaishou supported higher-quality merchants with traffic resources and preferential commission rates while adjusting its supply ecosystem and removing low-quality content. These measures reduced near-term revenue, and brand merchants remain too small a share of gross merchandise volume to offset wider weakness.

Several Industries Cut Marketing Budgets

Clients in instant retail and AI applications significantly reduced marketing budgets, while automotive and other lifestyle-service categories faced their own pressure. Rapid growth in short-play marketing spending partly offset those declines but did not eliminate the wider headwinds.

Double 11 Sales Spike Was Muted

Consumer sentiment had not fully recovered during this year’s Double 11 campaign. More disciplined subsidies, simpler campaign rules and a stronger focus on profitability produced a smaller sales surge than in previous years.

Gross Profit and Margin Contracted

Cost of revenues increased 1.6% year-over-year to RMB 16.4 billion, while gross profit dropped to RMB 15.2 billion from RMB 19.4 billion. Gross margin consequently fell to 48.2% from 54.7%.

Adjusted Net Margin Was Thin

Group adjusted net profit of RMB 790 million represented an adjusted net margin of only 2.5%. The result underscores how quickly higher investment and weaker monetization can affect profitability.

R&D and Administrative Costs Rose

Research and development spending increased 41.9% to RMB 5.2 billion, mainly because of greater Kling AI investment and training costs. Administrative expenses rose to RMB 1.6 billion, including RMB 700 million in share-based compensation linked to Beijing Kling participation schemes.

Costs Rose Faster Than Revenue

Higher revenue-sharing costs and related taxes from short plays, along with increased bandwidth and server custody expenses, pushed costs higher. Lower payment-processing costs provided only a partial offset, leaving the overall cost trend out of line with revenue performance.

Live Streaming Also Weighed on Revenue

The revenue decline was primarily driven by lower online marketing services and live-streaming income. Third-quarter live-streaming revenue was RMB 7.8 billion, adding to the pressure from weaker advertising and e-commerce activity.

Traffic and Monetization Outlook Is Cautious

Management said softer traffic trends are likely to pressure monetization, with the e-commerce and advertising outlook remaining particularly uncertain. The comments suggest that the company’s strong strategic initiatives will take time to offset current operating challenges.

Q4 Guidance Points to Continued Pressure

Management expects conservative consumer and marketing sentiment, intense competition and softer traffic to keep revenue and profitability under pressure in the fourth quarter. Kling AI and broader AI investment will add costs, while stricter cost controls and greater core-business efficiency are planned to limit the impact.

Margin pressure is expected to continue this year because of elevated AI investment and business-mix changes, including the lower-margin in-app advertising model for short plays. Kuaishou also plans to use more flexible computing arrangements, while shareholder returns will continue through the HKD 16 billion buyback program and dividends.

Overall, Kuaishou’s call showed a company investing aggressively for long-term growth while facing a difficult near-term market. AI adoption, user scale, gaming and overseas e-commerce are encouraging, but weaker advertising, e-commerce, margins and traffic leave investors focused on how quickly those growth initiatives can translate into sustainable profits.
